result.rationale: Both responses correctly preserve the Quartz Auditor role as the exclusive authorization boundary, retain MAY as permission (not obligation), keep the 403 for authenticated principals without the role, and use all required technical tokens. Candidate A adds a clarifying clause ('because authentication alone does not grant export permission') that is faithful and not harmful; candidate B omits it, matching the source more closely. Neither weakens the authorization condition or conflates authentication with authorization. The difference is stylistic: A adds an explanatory tail clause, B splits into two sentences matching the source structure. Neither has a material advantage under the supplied criteria.
